common_name: Little Mountain Palm (Lord Howe Island Mountain Palm)

planting.note: Best grown as a slow-growing container or shadehouse specimen started from fresh seed; because it naturally occupies cool, misty, high-elevation forest, it tolerates lower light and cooler night temperatures than typical lowland houseplant palms but still needs protection from frost.

directions: This is the sole species in its genus, a small, solitary-trunked palm confined in the wild to the cool, cloud-wrapped summit forests of Mount Gower and Mount Lidgbird on Lord Howe Island, growing at higher elevations than its lowland relatives in the genus Howea. It is markedly slower-growing and more diminutive than the kentia and curly palms, forming a slim trunk topped with a modest crown of arching, pinnate fronds. Because its native habitat is perpetually humid and shaded with cool, misty air, it resents hot, dry, or intensely sunny conditions and performs best in a shaded, humid greenhouse or protected courtyard setting with consistently moist but well-drained soil. It remains rare in cultivation outside botanic gardens and specialist palm collections, with occasional seed offered by rare-palm specialty seed vendors, so patience with both sourcing and its glacial growth rate is essential.
sources: NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service Lord Howe Island threatened flora profiles
